Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (answers at a high level)
- At-rest encryption: all customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for all control and data plane traffic; we recommend TLS 1.3 where supported.
- Customer-managed keys: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments via customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or HSM-based key wrapping. For Hosted API customers we offer envelope encryption with platform-managed keys by default; enterprise customers can discuss a private deployment for BYOK/HSM.
- Key material: Redwood does not store plaintext customer key material. We use key-wrapping and envelope encryption patterns; access to key operations is logged and auditable.

Hi Jordan —

Quick technical answers to your items — happy to walk through these on the call: 

- Persistence of key material: Redwood does not persist plaintext customer key material. For BYOK flows we store only wrapped keys (key-encryption-keys) and never the unwrapped key material. Key operations are proxied to the configured KMS/HSM.
- HSM support: We support integrations with Cloud KMS + CloudHSM (AWS KMS with CloudHSM, GCP KMS + Cloud HSM) for Dedicated/Private. For on-prem HSMs we support an HSM-backed key-wrapping gateway in Private deployments (customer provides HSM endpoints). Hosted customers: default is platform-managed keys with envelope encryption; for enterprise Hosted discussions we can assess a private tenancy or dedicated deployment to enable BYOK/HSM.
- Rotation & lifecycle: Automated rotation is supported for KEKs; customers can schedule rotations and trigger ad-hoc rotations via a management API. Rotation events are emitted to audit logs and to the observability console (token-level and key-operation logs).
- Audit & access logs: every key operation (encrypt/decrypt/wrap/unwrap) is timestamped, correlated with request IDs, and retained per our data retention policy (we can map retention windows for your procurement).

I’ll bring a short diagram and logs example to the architecture review. Confirming Tue 2026-08-25 11:00 PT works for me — sending invite via calendar.

Cheers,
